evidence_category: Fully formalized convergence and quantitative sum bounds for actual polynomial evaluation series
statement: Let A_n be actual complex multivariate polynomials homogeneous of degree n with L1(A_n)<=M*D^n. For D,r>=0 and D*r<1, the evaluation series is absolutely summable at each point of the literal closed complex polydisc of radius r, has a uniform sum there, its actual range partial sums converge uniformly, and its sum has norm at most M/(1-D*r). The theorem is generic in the variable index type, including Fin3. For Q_n homogeneous of degree n with L1(Q_n)<=M*D^(n+1), the same convergence conclusions hold with sum bound M*D/(1-D*r).
hypotheses: Only actual homogeneity, literal coefficient bounds, D/r nonnegativity and the strict geometric-ratio condition. No convergence, summability, analyticity or formal power-series representation hypothesis. The requested M>=0 cases are included; a separate M nonnegativity premise is unnecessary.
mathematical_change: The true degree n is retained in the geometric majorant. The shifted odd sequence pays the coefficient amplitude M*D and no additional radius factor. Boundary points of every admissible closed polydisc are included; D*r=1 is excluded.
manual_review: Both complete final source bodies, all six expanded declarations (the full 201-line log), every axiom report and the complete strict receipt were read directly. The actual evaluation bound source and pinned uniform-series/geometric majorant APIs were inspected. Independent review is owned by parent and is not asserted complete here.
trust: Only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no unexpected axioms, missing reports, printer failures, ellipses or forbidden source tokens.
environment: Lean 4.34.0-rc2 with pinned project object caches reused. No isolated source dependency rebuild claimed.

limits: No claim of analyticity of the limit is made here, nor of a physical KS identity for a particular series, quantitative descent in physical coordinates, global approximation, spectrum, solver correctness or full Theorem T.
